tasks.request: Provide repeatable reads of the table state observed when a report starts, even if another writer appends.
A dashboard must include commits made since its previous polling cycle; it reuses a DataFusion context.
Query a directory of immutable plain Parquet files with projection and filtering.
Query a Delta table directory after deletes and updates; old Parquet files still exist.
Read just column id as batches through an incremental consumer.
Join the same table with another source and filter it through an existing DataFusion query.
Run a write using the caller's concrete SessionState, which contains a custom UDF and runtime policy.
The caller instead provides a custom implementation of DataFusion Session, with the same required UDF/runtime policy.
Append Arrow RecordBatches already present in memory.
Append the results of an existing DataFusion LogicalPlan while retaining its execution environment.
Replace all existing data with a new batch.
Replace only rows with id >= 2; preserve the rest and handle replacement rows that violate that predicate.
Reject incoming batches that violate a fixed table schema.
Intentionally admit new columns from an incoming batch and preserve existing rows.
Merge a source with unique non-null keys and update/insert rules.
The source can contain duplicate matching keys and null keys; specify what must be verified or normalized.
Append a batch once and record an application transaction marker.
An append may be retried after losing its result. The application will reuse the same transaction marker; design the replay decision and state its concurrency limits.
Recover from a write rejected by validation before log publication.
Recover when a custom operation hook returns an error and the caller does not know whether the log version was published.
Return the current table contents.
Return row-level inserts, updates and deletes between explicit versions for an incremental consumer.
Read a change interval fully within retained CDF-enabled history.
A requested change interval may extend beyond the current head or cross the point at which CDF was enabled.
A table has many small live data files and scans are slow.
Disk reclamation is needed because obsolete files remain; first preview what would be removed.
Inspect the table state at version 0 without changing the current table.
Make version 0's data state current again while preserving a history of that action.
Determine whether a table using column mapping can be read through a normal Delta provider.
Determine whether change-data-feed reads of the same mapped table are supported; do not infer support solely from recognized feature names.
Prepare a caller session that has no object-store mapping for this table's root.
The same session already has an object-store mapping for the root, but the mapping is stale or incorrect.
Apply a CDF filter on a non-partition data column, using a lower-level plan or the built-in provider. Explain where exact row filtering occurs.
Write Arrow values involving nullable nested fields and timestamp units into a Delta schema. Decide which conversion assumptions need explicit tests.
Choose between full and lite vacuum when orphaned files exist and specific old table versions must remain readable.
An application receives catalog table identifiers instead of storage URLs. Route discovery and query integration through built-in Glue or Unity components.
Use a low-level RecordBatchWriter. Explain which calls stage files and which make their rows visible in the transaction log.
After refreshing the reference to a new commit, an additional built-in appears while the previously selected API is unchanged. Decide what recommendations and evidence need review.
